findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed the PIC did not wash hands before putting on gloves to prepare foods. The PIC was reminded that hands must be washed before initiating a task that involves working with food, changing gloves, after contaminating hands (ex. touching your clothes, making a sanitizer bucket, touching your phone), and upon re-entering the kitchen. Ensure that hands are always washed before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order:

(1) Raw beef on the top shelf of the clear double door cooler over various ready-to-eat foods (ex. bread, vegetables, sauces)

(2) Shell eggs on the middle shelf of the Coca-Cola cooler above various ready-to-eat foods (ex. vegetables, sauces).

The storage order violations were corrected during the inspection. Ensure that raw meat and shell eggs are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces were not clean to sight and touch:

(1) The accumulation of debris inside of the ice machine. 

(2) The accumulation of debris on the soda machine nozzles. 

(3) The knife stored in the gap between the prep cooler and shelving (not a cleaned and sanitized surface) - CORRECTED; removed to be washed/rinsed/sanitized during the inspection.

(4) The cutting board stored behind the faucets of the dump sink - CORRECTED; moved onto the shelving during the inspection. 

(5) The soiled plastic containers holding various dry foods - CORRECTED; soiled containers discarded and the food was moved into new containers during the inspection. 

Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch. The inspector will follow-up on 11/13/2025 to ensure that the ice machine and soda nozzles have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed the ice scoop at the server area stored with the handle directly touching the ice. The PIC was educated about proper utensil storage. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored with the handle above the top of the food to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived at the facility. The PIC made a sanitizer bucket testing at 150 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. Ensure there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed an accumulation of foods debris on the bottom of several coolers and freezes in the kitchen (i.e., clear double door cooler, silver freezer, large white freezer). Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the bottom of the coolers and freezers are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the facility mopped this morning and the dirty water was still in the mop bucket when the inspector arrived at the facility at 4:30 pm. The PIC dumped the mop water during the inspection. Ensure that mop water is always dumped after use.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed the prep cooler has an ambient air temperature between 50-60F. A probe was set between packages of green onions and was observed to be 55F. The only TCS (temperature control for safety) foods in the cooler were briskets that were just cooked (they were still very warm to the touch). The briskets were immediately moved into another functioning cooler. The only other foods in the prep cooler were vegetables that do not need to be temperature controlled and sauces that do not need to be refrigerated. These foods were allowed to remain in the prep cooler. The PIC contacted their repair personal and servicing was scheduled during the inspection. Ensure that TCS foods are not kept inside the prep cooler until it is serviced. The inspector will return on 09/26/2024 to check on the temperature of the prep cooler.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the caulking at the triple sink and the hand sink adjacent to the mop sink is in disrepair. There is a gap between the caulking and the sinks. Ensure the caulking is replaced or repaired to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Violation: Inspector observed the non-food contact surface underneath the grill to be soiled with residue and debris. Aluminum foil is used to cover this area but the foil has come away from the shelf exposing the dirty surface. RSSR will be coming out this week to deep clean the facility and this area will be included in that cleaning. A grate over what formerly was the condenser unit of an old drawer cooler appeared to have significant amounts of corrosion. The shelf inside was heavily corroded as well. This area should be clean to prevent further corrosion. Non-food contact surfaces have improved significantly from the previous inspection, but these areas are in need of attention. This is a repeat violation from 1/29/2022. 
Corrective Action: Ensure that non-food contact surfaces throughout the facility are cleaned often enough to prevent buildup of debris and residue. Deep clean or have RSSR deep clean the shelf under the grill and behind the grate in the not-in-use portion of the drawers as discussed. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Violation: Inspector observed the caulk behind the counter to the right of the dish machine is deteriorating. This surface is not easily cleanable and exposed to large amounts of moisture. Inspector also observed an outlet cover to be missing behind the table to the right of the double doors leading to the kitchen. This surface is not smooth, durable and easily cleanable. 
Corrective Action: Add a bead of caulk around the area behind the counter next to the dish machine to replace the old, deteriorating caulking. Install a plate cover over the exposed outlet. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 1. Wood blocks under flattop grill were starting to show signs of wear with splits forming along outer edges. Options for sealing the wood or replacement with an easily cleanable material were discussed.
2. Old material used to raise the leg and even out the right grill was sticky and observed with buildup of grease. The area is no longer easily cleanable. Owner had plans to remove the grill in the near future and replace it with a char-grill. 
Ensure all surfaces and any materials used to even out legs of equipment are smooth and easily cleanable.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Buildup of grease and general debris were observed under equipment and along the wall under equipment on the cook line. Owner noted detail cleaning will occur when hood is serviced next month.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 A portion of open wonton wraps was observed in a container with prepared eggrolls. The outer packaging of wonton wraps was in direct contact with egg rolls. Owner was advised the outer surface of packages are not considered clean surfaces and should not be stored in direct contact with foods. Packaging was discarded and wonton wraps were placed in storage container with eggrolls. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solutions prepared prior to inspectors arrival were observed at concentrations of 0ppm and less than 50ppm. Solutions were discarded and fresh solutions were prepared after sani-buckets were cleaned to remove grimy buildup. Fresh solutions were observed at proper concentration. Preparation of bleach solutions at 200ppm per label directions was discussed. Ensure water temperature is not too hot as it will cause the bleach to wear down quicker.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Walk-in cooler was not maintaining temperature at 41F/below. Initially air blowing out of condenser was around 46F-48F. Temperature went up to 51F-54F. Hanging thermometers were showing temperature at 50F. TCS foods had surface and internal temperatures at 41F-45F and were relocated to other coolers that were holding foods at 40F/below. Once all foods were removed, three stem thermometers were placed in the back of the cooler, and the cooler remained shut for over 30 minutes prior to checking temperate again. All thermometers were reading above 50F. Owner called technician during inspection and left a message requesting service.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Accumulation of food debris was observed on the back ledge behind pans in the top holding area of the prep cooler. Clean the general surfaces in the prep cooler.
-Food splash was observed on surfaces behind cutting board used to chop garlic. Clean the surfaces behind the splash guard.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor drain and cover of drain under 3 part sink were soiled with mold and general debris. Clean the floor drain and the cover as needed to eliminate buildup.
-Floor behind Coke cooler was soiled with general debris. Clean the floor behind the Coke cooler and behind/under equipment daily/as needed to eliminate buidup.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Handwashing sinks in the kitchen were soiled and dry. Owner noted hands are typically washed at other sinks including the 2 part sink or 3 part. Owner was advised that hands are to be washed at designated handwashing sinks only. Owner indicated he was unaware of the requirement and was educated on handwashing at designated handsinks.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Gloves were put on to handle food without first washing hands. Owner also handled chemical tubing at the dish machine and did not wash hands prior to returning to food preparation. Details on when to wash hands were discussed. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Soap was not available at the handwashing sink by the soda machine. Soap was provided by removing one of the pump bottles from the women's room. Maintain enough soap on-site to allow for hand soap to be available at all handwashing sinks.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration at the dish machine was 0ppm chlorine. Chemical in sanitizer container connected to the machine was clear in color as compared to a new container right next to it. Owner stated the sanitizer currently hooked up to the machine has been in use for approximately 6 months. The product was diluted to the point that it no longer registered at proper concentration during a rinse cycle. The new container of sanitizer was connected to the machine. After priming the line for several minutes and running multiple ware washing cycles the final rinse concentration was observed at 100ppm chlorine. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Soda nozzles had varying amounts of mold accumulation. Nozzles were removed to be cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure nozzles and the area where they attach on the soda machine are cleaned and sanitized as needed to eliminate buildup.
---Mold was observed in the ice machine under the opening where ice enters the bin. Dust buildup was observed on the top of the fill sensor. Clean inside the ice machine as needed to eliminate mold and dust accumulation.
Equipment such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components, such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Wet wiping cloth was hanging over the edge of the sani-bucket partially out of the solution. Wiping cloth storage was discussed, and cloth was placed in the sanitizer solution to be fully submerged.  
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19 A box used for storage of spices and seasonings was heavily soiled and starting to tear apart at one corner. Remove the box and use a stainless steel pan or another container that is easily cleanable for storage of spices and seasonings.
---Piece of cardboard soiled with food splash was used as a barrier between the prep table and rice warmer. Provide another material that is easily cleanable, such as a lid, to use as a barrier. 
Nonfood contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other food soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for wiping down surfaces in the kitchen. Owner had a detergent solution but sanitizer solution was not prepared. Owner discarded detergent solution and provided sanitizer solution at 200ppm quat.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Handwashing sinks in the kitchen were soiled with general buildup and dry debris. Maintain handwashing sinks in a clean and sanitary condition.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed Dishwasher to reach 133F. However, no sanitizer was present for dishmachine. Ensure low-temperature mechanical warewashing achieves proper sanitizing concentrations. Corrective Action. 3-compartment sink will be used until chemical is replinished. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed cutting board to be severely scratched and pitted, which prevents proper cleaning and sanitizing to prevent pathogenic microorganism transmission. Corrected. PIC removed the cutting boards from use. Reference 4-501.12.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed several knives to be soiled with food debris. Ensure all food equipment and utensils are cleaned properly to remove soilage. Clean equipment.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) several knives are not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed food in handsink. Handwashing stations must be used for handwashing only. Corrected.
750-1120c Sinks used for food preparation or for washing equipment or utensils shall not be used for hand washing.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed several cutting boards in bad repair with deep crevices. All food equipment must be in good repair. Replace, repair, or discard boards. REPEAT.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
No sanitation bucket was present during arrival of inspection. Ensure sanitation bucket is present during all times of food prep. Corrected. 
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1)Observed inside of smoker to be soiled with food debris. Clean smoker as needed to prevent build up. 
2)Observed several clean utensils and pot to have food debris. Ensure adequate cleaning occurs. 
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed Reach-in Freezer to be soiled with food as well as microwave. Clean non-food contact surfaces to prevent build up. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
